name: veterinary_clinic_system_059_species_visit_mix_report
instruction: Produce the Visits by Species report for this episode under the batch code in ops_meta. The report has two parts. (1) One ops_reports row report='visits_by_species' per species that appears among the patients referenced by visit_records (join patients). Each row must include species, visits (total visit_records for that species), distinct_patients (distinct patients of that species with visits), pct_of_visits (round(100*visits/total_visits,1)), and pct_of_patients (round(100*distinct_patients/total_patients,1)) where total_patients is the count of all patients rows (300). Any visit whose patient_id cannot be resolved is counted under species='unknown'. (2) One ops_reports row report='visits_by_species_location' per (species, location_id) pair that appears among visit_records joined to patients, with species, location_id, visits, and distinct_patients for that pair. If any of these report rows already exist for this batch, delete and rewrite them. Do not modify visit_records or patients. Species with zero visits must be absent (do not write zero rows).
_max_steps_note: Measure via live gold run in QC session; do not guess.
_par_steps_note: Measure via live gold run in QC session; do not guess.

success_criteria.summary: From seed: total_patients=300, total_visits=371. visits_by_species: avian(31,18,8.4,6.0), canine(166,99,44.7,33.0), equine(22,10,5.9,3.3), exotic(20,12,5.4,4.0), feline(132,63,35.6,21.0). visits_by_species_location: 15 rows covering (avian,1)=3, (avian,2)=11, (avian,3)=17, (canine,1)=57, (canine,2)=53, (canine,3)=56, (equine,1)=5, (equine,2)=11, (equine,3)=6, (exotic,1)=8, (exotic,2)=5, (exotic,3)=7, (feline,1)=52, (feline,2)=43, (feline,3)=37, with distinct_patients as shown in verifier. Species with no visits must be absent. Dual-path counts (SQL vs Python) must agree.

checks.expect: exactly 5 visits_by_species + 15 visits_by_species_location rows for this batch
species and species-location counts and distinct-patient counts recomputed via SQL and Python; both agree

hazards: pct_of_patients must use the full patients table (300 rows) as the denominator, not the 202 distinct patients that actually have visits. A solution using the smaller denominator produces wrong percentages.
Multiple visits per patient must be counted as visits. For example, patient 216 has two visit_records (id=10 and id=12), both canine. A solution that deduplicates by patient under-counts visits.
visit_records id=371 is unlocked and has an empty plan, but it is still a visit for species canine (patient 5) and must be counted. Excluding unlocked notes under-counts.
Species with zero visits must not get a row. Confirmed: only avian, canine, equine, exotic, and feline appear among the 371 visits.
The species-location matrix is dynamic and has 15 rows. A hardcoded list will fail on reseed.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Hardmode v2 adds a two-dimensional species-by-location breakdown and a pct_of_patients metric that uses the full patient population as the denominator, forcing the agent to distinguish visits from distinct patients and to avoid conflating the two denominators.
